chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Qul Huwa Allah Ahad' is a third of the Qur'an, and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun' is a fourth of the Qur'an.
ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Kafirun according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), stated that Surah al-Ikhlas constitutes one-third of the Qur'an and Surah al-Kafirun constitutes one-fourth. This highlights the immense virtue and weight of these two short chapters in Islamic worship and recitation. In Shia scholarly tradition, this narration underscores the centrality of Tawhid (monotheism) and Al-Ghulu (purity of belief from shirk) as the core themes of the entire Qur'an, justifying their frequent recitation in daily prayers.

en.ammaar-muslim: [6/1555] al-Kafi: Abu Ali al-Ash’ari from Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan b. Yahya from Ya’qub b. Shuayb from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:
My father صلوات الله عليه used to say: Qul Huwa l-Llāhu Aḥad is a third of the Qur’an, and, Qul Yā Ayyuhā l-Kāfirūn is a fourth of the Qur’an
